Viharamahadevi (Sinhala:විහාරමහාදේවි) was the mother of King Dutugamunu, Saddhatissa and the Queen consort of King Kavantissa (King of the Ruhuna Sri Lanka).According to recent findings her name might have been "Sharwaree" which means evening.
Queen Viharamahadevi was the daughter of King Kelanitissa who ruled Kelaniya.The King once punished an innocent monk by boiling him alive in a cauldron of oil. It is said that the gods, angered over this cruel deed, made the ocean rush inland and flood the land. Soothsayers said that if a princess was sacrificed to the sea, the raging waves would stop. The young princess sacrificed herself for the sins of her father and for the safety of her motherland. She was placed inside a beautifully decorated boat which bore the letters Daughter of a King and set adrift on the sea.
It is said that as soon as she was sent off, the sea suddenly turned calm again and the water receded. However, the King was very upset, the Queen was wailing and the citizens were very angry over the loss of their brave princess. They all started blaming the King.
Meanwhile, the young princess finally reached the shore, at a spot known as Dovera in Kirinda,in the southern part of the country, then known as Rohana (now Ruhuna) which was a quite prosperous area ruled by King Kavantissa. A fisherman who first spotted the boat is said to have run to the castle, and informed the King about the castaway princess. The Thupavamsa says birds who first spotted the floating boat informed the King.
The princess was brought before the King in a procession. The King, on hearing her story, was so impressed that he decided to marry the princess who had been so brave and patriotic to sacrifice her life for her country. As a part of the legend it's said as she reached the shore at a spot close to the Lanka Vihara, she was named Viharamahadevi. The place where she landed is marked with an inscription laid there by Prince Mahanaga.
She bore the King two sons, Dutugemunu and Saddhatissa. The former is one of the greatest heroes of Sri Lanka, while Viharamahadevi herself is recognised as a great heroine of Sri Lanka.

Rumassala Sanctuary is a popular tourist destination located on Jungle Beach Road, Unawatuna, Galle. The sanctuary is a botanical paradise with rare plants and medicinal plants as well as endemic birds. It is situated in the vicinity of the legendary Mount Rumassala associated with the epic "Ramayana". Rumassala is believed to be part of the Himalayas.

Rumassala Sanctuary: Historical Significance

The "Ramayana" narrates that Hanumanta threw a piece of the Himalayas here. It is also known as one of the main and historical places used to transport large quantities of spices, minerals and precious stones for long sea voyages thousands of years ago. Near the sanctuary is a small cemetery which is known as a resting place for many British civil servants and sailors of the time.

Arrival at Rumassala Sanctuary

From Galle, you can travel along Matara Road past Dewat to Unawatuna and reach Valle through Dewalaya Road (Yaddehimulla Road). And both can be reached from the road near the cement factory.

The beautiful Athamala falls in Matara district is created by Nilwala Ganga and this is known as the only waterfall of Nilwala Ganga. This is also known as Pahurutota Falls. With the water of Nilwala river, this beautiful waterfall is a wonderful creation of nature at a height of about 52 meters. This waterfall with beautiful surroundings is not a suitable place for bathing.

The closest town to the waterfall is Pitabeddara. You can use Pitabeddara Siyambalagoda road or Nil Ella Vatuya road to reach this waterfall. Both the roads join at the Athamala junction and after passing 3 km from there meet the Athamala Falls. In the past, there was an elephant market at this place, so elephants used to hang out here and one day an elephant going from this market fell down the falls and died, so this place got its name as Elephanta Falls, according to legend. This waterfall falls down into two parts and from the upper part the stream falls down and the water flows down freely creating the second waterfall. In the second part, the water falls down and creates a large pool of water.

The beach is surrounded by lush greenery and stunning rock formations, and the crystal-clear waters are perfect for swimming and snorkeling. The beach is relatively undeveloped, and there are no restaurants or other amenities available, so it's best to bring your own snacks and drinks.

One of the unique features of Matara Paravi Duwa Beach is the small island located just off the coast. This island, known as Paravi Duwa, is accessible by a small wooden bridge and is a great spot to take in the stunning views of the beach and the surrounding coastline.

The beach is relatively quiet and secluded, which adds to its charm and natural beauty. The lack of amenities and development also gives visitors a chance to experience the authentic Sri Lankan beach experience.

However, it's important to note that there are no lifeguards on duty at the beach, so visitors should exercise caution when swimming or snorkeling. It's also a good idea to bring your own sunscreen and hat to protect yourself from the sun, as there is limited shade available on the beach.
